title: Choose Roster's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Office Wall Calendar. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Sketches show the payroll run review screen.

options.label: Office Wall Calendar
options.lineage: printed company wall calendars: sponsor masthead, big day numerals, public holidays in red
options.thesis: Every payroll fact is pinned to a date, read the way everyone reads the calendar on the office wall.
options.viewport: Run review under a green masthead; the period header is October's month sheet with red holidays and 21 working days counted; the employee table below; each figure's base, rate and rule version in a margin column.
options.risk: Calendar motifs can turn decorative; the date strip must do real work (proration, effective dates) or it becomes a theme.

raised.raise: Spans are drawn at exact length on the day grid: a 3-day leave is 3 cells, a rule version runs to its exact end date.
Each number carries its working in a margin column (base, rate, cap, rule version) instead of a tooltip.
Every run, rule version and payslip carries a sequential document number as its primary identifier.
Neutrals follow one strict stepped tonal scale; no ad-hoc greys.
Review progress is marked per employee: checked rows ticked, flagged rows circled, state kept.

options.label: Countersigned Form
options.lineage: office approval forms with two signature boxes and rubber stamps
options.thesis: Every irreversible step is a form that two people sign; the stamp is the state.
options.viewport: Run review as a form: approval boxes 0/2 at top right, totals as filled form fields, employee table below.
options.risk: The most familiar HR artifact; stamps can read kitsch if used beyond approvals. This is also where most runs in this category land.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.lineage: airport departure boards and segmented boarding passes
options.thesis: Payroll changes behave like gate changes: they move in place and stay lit until someone has noticed.
options.viewport: Run review as a board: employees ranked by change vs last month, changed rows lit amber until acknowledged; the selected payslip as a segmented pass on the right.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and holds product clarity (difference review is the core task); loses on audience identification, since HR does not live in airports.
options.risk: Reads as a travel app if the board styling goes beyond rows and one alert colour.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Setting
options.thesis: Text columns round a rail of keys, apparatus in the margin.
options.viewport: Two narrow columns with a vermilion key rail.
options.case: Too literary for HR managers and lands in the bone-and-vermilion rut.
options.risk: Reads as a book, not a payroll tool.
options.kept: Margin apparatus: every figure's working sits beside it.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Shape is action, length is exact duration.
options.case: No identification for HR; vertical time hurts table reading.
options.kept: Length is exact duration: spans drawn to true length on the day grid.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything is a numbered catalog entry.
options.viewport: Black field, one plot, a fac number.
options.case: Too artsy and coded for trust-first HR screens.
options.kept: Sequential document numbers as primary identifiers.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.lineage: printer's exposure cards and zone ramps
options.thesis: Load as hatch density on stacked sheets.
options.viewport: Overlapping sheets over a zone ramp.
options.case: Overlapping sheets fight dense tables; low identification.
options.kept: One stepped tonal scale for all neutrals.

options.label: Convention Circle Catalog
options.thesis: Stamp-sized cells in a numbered hall grid.
options.viewport: Packed thumbnail grid with hall map.
options.case: Hobby-culture register clashes with payroll trust.
options.kept: Marked review state: ticked and circled rows that persist.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What modern HR SaaS ships (Rippling, Personio, BambooHR), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Side navigation, run summary cards, sortable employee table.
